primitives.name: permutation_invariant_triplet
primitives.math_basis: Group theory: consider the symmetric group S_6 acting on the 6 drawn positions. Under the hypothesis that draws are simultaneous field manifestations (time does not exist), the labeling of positions 1..6 is arbitrary -- the draw is an unordered multiset. We test whether certain triplets of numbers exhibit permutation-invariant correlations: if triplet {a,b,c} appears together, then any permutation of their roles (which appeared in position 1 vs 2 vs 3) should carry no predictive information beyond the set membership itself. Deviation from this symmetry would indicate positional structure imposed by a field.
primitives.implementation: For each triplet of numbers (a,b,c), compute the joint appearance frequency F(a,b,c). Then decompose into marginal single-appearance frequencies f(a), f(b), f(c). Define invariant_score = F(a,b,c) / (f(a)*f(b)*f(c)). If draws are truly random-unordered, this ratio should be ~1 for all triplets. Systematic deviations -- especially structured ones forming subgroups of S_3 -- signal non-random field structure. For scoring individual number n: average invariant_score over all triplets containing n, weighted by triplet frequency. High score = number participates in permutation-invariant clusters.
primitives.why_different: Existing primitives measure frequency, co-occurrence, or periodicity -- all statistical correlations in a temporal sequence. This primitive tests GROUP-THEORETIC STRUCTURE: whether the draw mechanism respects permutation symmetry. It does not ask 'do these numbers appear together more often?' but rather 'does their joint appearance follow the symmetry pattern expected from an unordered field manifestation?' This is a structural hypothesis test, not a statistical one.
primitives.expected_signature: Triplet invariant scores will form distinct clusters (not a smooth distribution). Numbers belonging to the same cluster will have correlated invariant scores across all triplets they share. The cluster structure will be stable across time windows of different sizes (scale-invariant clustering), indicating a field-determined grouping rather than statistical fluctuation.

primitives.name: modular_ring_spectrum
primitives.math_basis: Ring theory: for modulus m in {7, 11, 13}, map each number n in {1..33} to its residue class n mod m. The ring Z_m partitions the number space into m residue classes. Under pure randomness, each draw of 6 numbers from 33 produces a residue multiset that follows a hypergeometric distribution. However, if the lottery is determined by a field structure, the residue multisets will exhibit systematic bias -- certain residue combinations will appear with probability significantly different from hypergeometric expectation. We analyze the joint distribution across multiple moduli simultaneously, treating (n mod 7, n mod 11, n mod 13) as a CRT-encoded signature for each number.
primitives.implementation: Step 1: For each modulus m in [7, 11, 13], compute observed residue-class frequency matrix O_m[r] = count of draws where residue r appeared, versus expected E_m[r] from hypergeometric model. Compute chi-squared statistic chi2_m for each modulus. Step 2: Compute cross-modulus correlation: for each pair (m1, m2), compute the joint residue distribution and test independence. Step 3: For number n, its modular_ring_score = weighted combination of (O_m[n%m] - E_m[n%m]) / sqrt(E_m[n%m]) across all three moduli, plus bonus for cross-modulus correlation alignment. Step 4: Apply Chinese Remainder Theorem encoding: the triplet (n%7, n%11, n%13) uniquely identifies n for n < 1001. Analyze whether draws cluster in CRT-space.
primitives.why_different: Existing modulo primitives (ModuloClassDistribution) simply check if a number's residue class has been frequent recently -- a frequency-based approach. This primitive uses RING-THEORETIC structure: it tests whether the algebraic structure of Z_7 x Z_11 x Z_13 carries predictive information. It examines whether draws are concentrated in specific regions of CRT-encoded space, which would indicate the field has structure aligned with these modular arithmetic properties. This is testing whether the field 'respects' certain modular symmetries.
primitives.expected_signature: CRT-encoded space will show non-uniform density: certain residue-triplet regions will be overrepresented. The chi-squared statistics will be consistently significant across multiple time windows. Cross-modulus correlations will be non-zero and stable. The pattern will be self-consistent: if (a%7, a%11, a%13) predicts well, then (b%7, b%11, b%13) for nearby b will show related structure (not independent).

primitives.name: cooccurrence_graph_clustering
primitives.math_basis: Graph theory: construct a weighted co-occurrence graph G = (V, E) where V = {1..33} and edge weight w(i,j) = co-occurrence frequency of numbers i and j across historical draws. Apply spectral graph theory: compute the adjacency matrix A, derive the normalized Laplacian L = I - D^(-1/2)AD^(-1/2), and examine its eigenvalues and eigenvectors. If the lottery has non-random field structure, the graph will exhibit community structure (block-diagonal adjacency pattern) detectable via spectral clustering. Random graphs have characteristic eigenvalue distributions (Wigner semicircle for Erdos-Renyi, power-law for Barabasi-Albert). Deviation from these distributions indicates structured connectivity.
primitives.implementation: Step 1: Build adjacency matrix A from co-occurrence data over sliding windows (30, 100, 300 periods). Step 2: Compute normalized Laplacian L and its first k eigenvectors (k=3..6). Step 3: Apply k-means clustering on the eigenvector embedding (spectral clustering). Step 4: Evaluate cluster quality using modularity Q = (1/2m) * sum_ij [A_ij - E_ij] * (c_i == c_j) where E_ij is expected edge weight under null model. Step 5: For number n, its clustering_score = (a) modularity contribution when n is included, (b) cluster cohesion = average edge weight to same-cluster members, (c) inter-cluster isolation = inverse of average edge weight to other-cluster members. High score = tightly clustered with strong isolation from other clusters.
primitives.why_different: Existing relational primitives (CooccurrenceAffinity, MutualExclusionScore) treat co-occurrence as pairwise statistics. This primitive treats the ENTIRE co-occurrence structure as a GRAPH and applies spectral graph theory. It does not ask 'is n correlated with these specific numbers?' but rather 'does n belong to a community structure in the full co-occurrence network?' This captures higher-order structure: three numbers might have weak pairwise correlations but strong collective co-occurrence, forming a triangle that pairwise analysis misses.
primitives.expected_signature: The Laplacian spectrum will show eigenvalue gaps (spectral gaps) indicating clear community structure. Modularity Q will be significantly above the random-graph baseline (~0.3-0.5 vs ~0.1 for random). Clusters will be stable across different time windows (30, 100, 300 periods). The community assignment for each number will be consistent, suggesting field-determined groupings rather than statistical noise.

primitives.name: self_similar_gap_series
primitives.math_basis: Fractal geometry / self-similarity: if the field structure operates simultaneously at all temporal scales (time does not exist), then patterns observed at one scale should repeat at other scales. We analyze the gap series (inter-arrival times) for each number n. Under randomness, gap series follow a geometric distribution with no scale-invariant structure. Under field determinism, the gap series will exhibit self-similarity: the pattern of gaps at scale S will be statistically similar to the pattern at scale k*S for various k. We quantify this using the Hurst exponent H from rescaled range (R/S) analysis. H > 0.5 indicates persistent long-range dependence (fractal structure); H = 0.5 is pure randomness; H < 0.5 is anti-persistent.
primitives.implementation: Step 1: For each number n, construct binary appearance sequence s[t] = 1 if n drawn at t, 0 otherwise. Step 2: Compute cumulative deviation curve X[t] = sum(s[i] - E) for i=1..t where E = overall frequency. Step 3: For each scaling factor r in {5, 10, 20, 40, 80}, divide the series into n_r = N/r non-overlapping segments. For each segment, compute range R_r = max(X) - min(X) and standard deviation S_r. Step 4: Compute average R/S ratio across segments for each r. Step 5: Fit log(R/S) = log(c) + H*log(r) via linear regression. The slope H is the Hurst exponent. Step 6: Score for number n = |H - 0.5| * 2, capped at 1.0. Numbers with H significantly != 0.5 (especially H > 0.6 or H < 0.4) get high scores, indicating non-random fractal structure.
primitives.why_different: Existing primitives measure frequency, periodicity, or omission -- all point-wise or pairwise statistics. This primitive tests whether the ENTIRE temporal structure of a number's appearance exhibits SCALE-INVARIANCE. A number with H=0.73 has long-range persistent correlations that no frequency or periodicity analysis can detect. This is fundamentally different: it tests whether the number's appearance pattern is a fractal object, which would be evidence of a field mechanism operating simultaneously across all time scales.
primitives.expected_signature: Hurst exponents for winning numbers will systematically deviate from 0.5 (the random baseline). The deviation will be consistent across multiple time windows. Different numbers will show correlated Hurst exponents (belonging to the same fractal family). Self-similarity will hold across scales: the gap pattern at 10-period resolution will be statistically indistinguishable (after normalization) from the pattern at 100-period resolution.

primitives.name: entropy_deficit_indicator
primitives.math_basis: Information theory: for a truly random uniform process drawing 6 from 33, the Shannon entropy per draw is H_max = log2(C(33,6)) = log2(1,107,568) = 20.09 bits. Any deterministic or semi-deterministic field mechanism will produce draws with LOWER entropy because the outcome space is effectively restricted. We measure entropy deficit in three ways: (a) single-draw entropy: does the actual distribution of draw outcomes concentrate on a subset of C(33,6) possibilities? (b) conditional entropy: H(X_t | X_{t-1}, ..., X_{t-k}) < H(X_t) indicates memory. (c) per-number entropy: the marginal entropy of each number's appearance sequence deviates from Bernoulli(log(6/33)).
primitives.implementation: Step 1 (Draw-level): Bin all historical draws into feature vectors (sum, odd-even ratio, high-low ratio, span, largest gap, modulo-7 signature). Count frequency of each bin. Compute Shannon entropy H_features = -sum(p_i * log2(p_i)). Compare to maximum H_max = log2(N_bins). Deficit = H_max - H_features. Large deficit = concentrated feature space = non-random. Step 2 (Conditional): For each number n, compute P(n appears | last_k_draws_feature) for various feature windows. If conditional probability varies significantly from marginal probability (computed via mutual information I(X_n; Y_last_k)), this indicates memory/structure. Step 3 (Per-number): For each n, compute empirical entropy of its binary appearance sequence: H_n = -p*log2(p) - (1-p)*log2(1-p) where p = freq(n). Compare to Bernoulli entropy at p=6/33. Step 4: composite_score(n) = weighted combination of (a) mutual information with past, (b) entropy deviation from Bernoulli, (c) participation in low-entropy feature bins.
primitives.why_different: Existing primitives are all frequency-based or correlation-based -- they measure specific statistical patterns. This primitive measures INFORMATION-THEORETIC STRUCTURE: it asks whether the draw process has LESS uncertainty than maximum randomness would predict. It does not look for specific patterns but measures the ABSENCE of randomness itself. A process can be completely non-random while having no detectable frequency bias, periodicity, or correlation -- yet it will still have lower entropy than maximum. This is the most fundamental test of non-randomness.
primitives.expected_signature: Feature-space entropy will be significantly below maximum (e.g., H_features = 12 bits vs H_max = 18 bits for 262,144 bins). Mutual information between consecutive draws will be non-zero and consistent. Per-number entropy will show bimodal distribution: some numbers have H_n close to Bernoulli-maximum (appearing randomly) while others have H_n << Bernoulli-maximum (appearing with structure). The entropy deficit will persist across all time windows, not diminish with more data (as statistical fluctuations would).
